gap: The boat must visibly interact with the water. Check for a bow wave and side spray sheet peeling off the hull. Behind it there must be a turbulent foam trail with ragged, streaky edges that spreads into a V and fades into churned water, not a flat white band with a straight edge. Airborne spray must read as translucent mist or streaked droplets. Fail if any crisp, opaque, round white dot is visible.

Judge: The commercial frames win clearly in all four pairs: pair 1 B, pair 2 B, pair 3 A and pair 4 A. None of the four is close. Water shading is where the in-development game comes closest. It has good teal colour, normal-mapped ripples, clean planar reflections of the towers, and in pair 4 a sun-glint streak and several boat wakes. Two areas are far below AAA. First, how the water reacts to boats and the shore: spray is opaque white dot sprites, wakes are flat white bands with hard edges, foam uses an obvious Voronoi cell pattern, ripple rings are perfectly geometric, and hulls show no bow-wave displacement. Second, the world around the water: placeholder box buildings, cloned towers with identical window textures, flat untextured brown ground, sparse trees and traffic, no people, and empty horizons where the world visibly ends. Lighting is also flat, with no readable sun, long shadows, layered haze or lens effects, and the commercial frames rely on exactly those for atmosphere. The fixes that would help most are: (1) rebuild foam, wake and spray as turbulent, streaky, translucent effects that dissipate gradually, and (2) fill every land surface with varied, textured, populated geometry, adding atmospheric haze toward the horizon. The commercial frames in pairs 2, 3 and 4 genuinely wow. Pair 1 B is a competent but ordinary promotional shot. Methodology note: the commercial images in pairs 1 and 3 carry a visible game-logo watermark in the corner, so those two pairs are not truly blind. My verdicts would be the same without the logo, but the watermark should be cropped out of future comparison sets.
